name: english_05
context: An English tweet from the SemEval-2017 sentiment analysis dataset. The tweets were found by searching Twitter for popular topics of the time, such as public figures, products, places, events and political issues, and were posted between 2012 and early 2017. At least five crowd workers labelled the overall sentiment of each tweet.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 0 scored 71.6 macro-F1. The weakest label is neutral: only 118 of 207 neutral tweets were labelled neutral, with 45 going to negative and 44 to positive. A further 35 positive tweets went to neutral.

Neutral tweets called negative mostly hold mild, analytical or joking criticism rather than real upset:
- sports commentary ("Fake punt on 4th and 11? Wow", "folds up like a lawnchair", Josh Hamilton "Lol");
- political remarks (Jeb/Cantor, Kerry);
- sarcasm framed as banter;
- complaints about trivial plans (no Grey's on Thursday, dorm money, netflix tonight);
- matter-of-fact news of executions or RIP mentions.
The annotators keep these neutral unless the author is clearly angry, hurt or hostile.

Neutral tweets called positive are mostly personal plans and activities (seeing a film, going to a concert, eating deep-fried food, "who wants to come"). They get positive only with overt enthusiasm or praise.

Positive tweets called neutral are upbeat promotional or news items about something the author favours (gala, season kick-off, Apple Watch case, a team playing well, a trend listing). That direction is noisy, so I will only nudge it.

Changes for version 1:
- Raise the bar for negative to clear upset or hostility.
- Send mild critique, banter, opinionated sports analysis and trivial complaints to neutral.
- Mark tributes and memorials as positive, and plain death or execution news as neutral unless the tweet is about a violent attack.
- Require explicit emotional wording for positive on personal plans.
- Keep upbeat promotion as positive.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 1 over-corrected and fell from 71.6 to 64.3 macro-F1. Negative recall collapsed (107 negative tweets went to neutral) and 70 positive tweets went to neutral. The annotators count mild tilt in both directions. Complaints, disappointment, sports criticism, sarcastic jabs, and bad news such as injuries or legal trouble are negative. Mild interest, fun plans, good news about a favoured team or person, and upbeat promotion are positive. Neutral should be kept for texts with no evaluative tilt. Version 2 returns near the version 0 balance and states this explicitly. This rewrite also trims examples and wording to get under 400 words.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 2 (68.5) leaned too far toward sentiment. Neutral recall fell to 87 of 207, with 58 neutral tweets called positive and 62 called negative. Version 0 (71.6) had the best balance, and version 1 showed that strong neutral pressure destroys negative and positive recall.

Neutral tweets called negative in version 2 were mostly:
- analytical sports or political commentary (Fake punt, Josh Hamilton, Simmons ranking, Kerry, Jeb/Cantor);
- reported news with bad elements but no author feeling (McGregor knee, Daesh warning, Boko Haram oil);
- jokey self-deprecating gripes about trivial things (no TV on Tuesday nights, netflix tonight, dorm money, put Twilight on);
- hypothetical feelings.

Neutral tweets called positive were mostly:
- personal plans and activities stated without explicit feeling words (going to a concert, eating, watching a show);
- venue or bar ads with calls to action ('Don't miss', 'Check out').

Plan for version 3:
- Start from the version 0 balance.
- Make the test whether the feeling is the point of the tweet. A clear stance or emotion gets positive or negative. Passing evaluation inside commentary, plain plans, routine ads and trivial joking gripes get neutral.
- Keep bad-news negative for real harm to people (injuries, deaths, attacks, charges) reported with concern, but not for neutral analysis.
- Avoid the over-correction of version 1 by keeping clear complaints and disappointment as negative.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!
Pretty Little Liars isn’t back on till January. What am I supposed to do with my Tuesday nights until then?
Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!
Pretty Little Liars isn’t back on till January. What am I supposed to do with my Tuesday nights until then?

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 4 scored 70.4, below version 3's 71.8. Pushing ads, promos and event plans toward positive added 44 neutral-to-positive errors. Its negative guidance did help: negative tweets lost to neutral fell from 44 to 29. Version 5 keeps that negative guidance and reverts promos and plans to neutral unless the author shows explicit enthusiasm. It adds only a narrow positive extension for achievements, honours and welcome news. This rewrite is trimmed to stay under 400 words.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 5 is the best so far at 73.4. Positive recall is still weak, with 54 positive tweets labelled neutral. Many of these fall into two groups.

Personal outings with a clear treat, a loved one or a stated desire:
- on our way to Foo Fighters
- surprising mom with AC/DC tickets
- Disneyland with Moonbyul
- homecoming that should be fun
- Sam Smith with my sister
- 'I really want to go'
- 'be my date'

Tech and product launches or new features:
- Apple Watch now works with smart lock
- waterproof case
- Apple event coverage and keynote hint
- setting up a Galaxy Note 5

Neutral counterparts are bare check-ins ('I'm going to Clutch at Buster's - Dec 28'), bar and venue ads, and plans with hedging or indifference ('hoping it does the book justice', 'haven't really listened to him lol').

I will make a small, targeted shift:
- Outings framed as a treat, as shared with someone special, or as something the author wants to do become positive.
- New tech and product features or launches become positive.
- Bare check-ins, venue ads and indifferent plans stay neutral.

Neutral-to-negative errors (39) are mostly fan commentary on players and coaches (lawnchair, Josh Hamilton, Brook Lopez) and some news of harm (McGregor knee, Yakub execution). Gold labels are inconsistent here, so I only add a light note: second-guessing play without insults or anger is neutral.

All other wording stays close to version 5, kept under 400 words.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 6 is the best so far at 73.9. Version 7 makes small targeted additions:
- Tributes, vigils and support gatherings are positive even after a tragedy.
- Fans mocking a rival are positive.
- Joking critique of a player's play is neutral.
- Self-reports of watching, playing or bingeing without praise are neutral.

This rewrite trims the wording to fit under 400 words.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 8 returns to version 6, the best so far at 73.9. It adds mild interest in or approval of a product, show or service as positive, and drops the vigil clause from version 7. The Apple Watch example is removed to fit under 400 words; the new-feature cue in the rule and cues still covers it.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 8 is the best so far at 74.1, with errors spread fairly evenly across the confusion matrix. Most remaining errors look like annotator noise. The same patterns go both ways: media eagerness is labelled positive in some tweets and neutral in others, and critique is labelled neutral in some and negative in others.

One fairly consistent pattern among negative tweets called neutral is mixed reviews of a film, show, album or game that end on a complaint:
- 'it was good I guess but... it bothered me'
- 'very unrealistic. The 1st movie was better'
- 'alright doesn't even compete with future'
- 'I can't even play lol'

So version 9 makes one minimal change: mixed reviews that end on a complaint count as negative. Everything else stays as in version 8, with slight trimming to stay under 400 words.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 9 tied version 8 at 74.1. The mixed-review clause recovered 8 negative tweets, but neutral tweets called negative rose from 32 to 38. The balanced Kanye tweet ('insane... may be a complete genius... still don't want him to be president') also flipped to negative. For this final version I keep version 9 but replace one neutral example with the balanced Kanye tweet, so balanced judgements stay neutral and only reviews that end on a complaint go to negative. Wording is trimmed to stay under 400 words.
next_examples_not_copied: Can't wait to see you tomorrow at The Roxy!
